title: The Bus That Waited
summaryZh: 哈金開了十一年的九號公車,每天早上都會在第三站多等兩分鐘。公司裝上準點計分螢幕之後,他被叫進了辦公室。

daily.seriesTitle: Two Minutes on the North Road

sentences.text: Hakim had driven the number nine bus along the north road for eleven years.
sentences.zh: 哈金在北路上開九號公車已經十一年了。

sentences.text: The route began at the town square and ended at the last farm before the hills.
sentences.zh: 這條路線從鎮上的廣場開始,一直到山腳下最後一座農場為止。

sentences.text: He knew every turn, every hole in the road, and every passenger by name.
sentences.zh: 每個轉彎、路上每個坑洞,還有每位乘客的名字,他都記得。

sentences.text: He also knew that Mrs. Oyelaran was always going to be late.
sentences.zh: 他也知道歐耶拉蘭太太一定會遲到。

sentences.text: She lived in a green house with a heavy iron gate, just past the third stop.
sentences.zh: 她住在第三站再過去一點,一棟有著沉重鐵門的綠色房子裡。

sentences.text: Most mornings she came through that gate at the exact moment the bus was pulling away.
sentences.zh: 多數的早晨,她走出那道鐵門時,公車正好要開走。

sentences.text: So, without telling anyone, Hakim started waiting for her.
sentences.zh: 於是哈金沒有告訴任何人,就開始等她。

sentences.text: He would stop the bus, open the door, and count slowly to one hundred and twenty.
sentences.zh: 他會把車停下、打開車門,然後慢慢數到一百二十。

sentences.text: Two minutes, and never a second more than that.
sentences.zh: 就兩分鐘,一秒都不會多。

sentences.text: In eleven years, not one passenger had ever complained about those two minutes.
sentences.zh: 這十一年來,沒有任何一位乘客抱怨過那兩分鐘。

sentences.text: Then the company put a small screen on the panel beside his seat.
sentences.zh: 後來公司在他座位旁的面板上裝了一個小螢幕。

sentences.text: It showed a single number, and that number was his punctuality score.
sentences.zh: 螢幕上只顯示一個數字,那個數字就是他的準點分數。

sentences.text: Green meant that he was on time, and red meant that he was late.
sentences.zh: 綠色代表他準時,紅色代表他遲到。

sentences.text: By the end of the first week, his screen was red every single morning.
sentences.zh: 第一週結束時,他的螢幕每天早上都是紅的。

sentences.text: Drivers began comparing their scores in the yard, and Hakim stopped joining them.
sentences.zh: 司機們開始在車場裡比分數,哈金就不再加入他們了。

sentences.text: On Friday, the dispatcher asked him to come into the office before his shift.
sentences.zh: 星期五,調度員請他上班前先到辦公室一趟。

sentences.text: "You lose two minutes at stop three," she said. "Every day, for years."
sentences.zh: 「你在第三站少了兩分鐘,」她說。「每一天,而且好幾年了。」

sentences.text: Hakim explained about the green house and the gate that opened so slowly.
sentences.zh: 哈金解釋了那棟綠色房子,還有那道開得很慢的鐵門。

sentences.text: He said that it was only two minutes, and that the bus always caught up.
sentences.zh: 他說那只有兩分鐘,而且公車後面總是追得回來。

sentences.text: The dispatcher listened to all of it without once interrupting him.
sentences.zh: 調度員從頭到尾聽完,一次也沒有打斷他。

sentences.text: Then she turned her own screen around so that he could see it.
sentences.zh: 然後她把自己的螢幕轉過來,讓他看得見。

sentences.text: "Look at the card data," she said quietly.
sentences.zh: 「你看一下刷卡紀錄,」她輕聲說。

sentences.text: Every passenger touched a card to the reader when they got on the bus.
sentences.zh: 每位乘客上車時都要把卡片碰一下感應機。

sentences.text: Mrs. Oyelaran's card had not been used once in the last three weeks.
sentences.zh: 歐耶拉蘭太太的卡片,在過去三個星期裡一次都沒有用過。

sentences.text: Hakim looked at the empty row of dates for a long time.
sentences.zh: 哈金盯著那排空白的日期看了很久。

sentences.text: Every morning he had been holding the door open for someone who was no longer coming.
sentences.zh: 他每天早上把門開著等的,是一個再也不會來的人。

sentences.text: He could not think of a single thing to say.
sentences.zh: 他一句話也想不出來。

sentences.text: The dispatcher waited, and then she said something he had not expected at all.
sentences.zh: 調度員等了一會兒,然後說了一句他完全沒想到的話。

sentences.text: "I am not asking you to stop waiting. I am asking you to tell me why."
sentences.zh: 「我不是要你別再等了。我是要你告訴我為什麼。」

sentences.text: So Hakim told her.
sentences.zh: 於是哈金告訴了她。

sentences.text: He told her about the iron gate, and about the eleven years behind it.
sentences.zh: 他說了那道鐵門,也說了鐵門背後那十一年。

sentences.text: He told her that in three weeks, nobody at all had gone to check on the old woman.
sentences.zh: 他說,這三個星期以來,根本沒有任何人去看看那位老太太。

sentences.text: The dispatcher wrote the address down on a piece of paper and folded it.
sentences.zh: 調度員把地址寫在一張紙上,然後折了起來。

sentences.text: "Go and drive your route," she said. "I will make a call this morning."
sentences.zh: 「你去開你的車吧,」她說。「我今天早上會打通電話。」

sentences.text: That day Hakim stopped at the third stop exactly as he always had.
sentences.zh: 那天,哈金還是跟以前一樣停在第三站。

sentences.text: He opened the door to an empty pavement and counted to one hundred and twenty.
sentences.zh: 他對著空無一人的人行道打開車門,數到一百二十。

sentences.text: The waiting felt different now, but he did not believe that it was wrong.
sentences.zh: 現在這樣的等待感覺不一樣了,但他不覺得這樣做是錯的。

questions.q: Why did Hakim stop for two extra minutes at the third stop?
options: Because Mrs. Oyelaran was usually late reaching the bus
Because the company told drivers to wait there
Because the road ahead was often blocked

questions.q: What did the card data show the dispatcher?
options: That Mrs. Oyelaran had not taken the bus for three weeks
That Hakim had been arriving early at every other stop
That more passengers were using stop three than before

questions.q: What did the dispatcher want from Hakim?
options: An explanation, not an end to the waiting
A promise that he would never wait again
A new route with fewer stops on it
